artists.biography: Tennis was an American indie pop band from Denver made up of husband-and-wife duo Alaina Moore and Patrick Riley. The duo formed in 2010 and released their debut album, Cape Dory, in 2011. A second album, Young & Old, was released in 2012. Their third album, Ritual in Repeat (2014), was released on Communion Records.

perplexity.description:
Pollen is the sixth studio album by American indie-pop duo Tennis, released on February 10, 2023, through their own label Mutually Detrimental. The album continues Tennis’s signature blend of melodic pop and subtle electronic textures, characterized by shimmering synths, crisp rhythms, and Alaina Moore’s distinctive vocals. While rooted in the duo’s established sound, Pollen introduces slightly more distorted guitar tones and a punchier production style, lending the record a livelier, more dynamic feel compared to their earlier, more subdued works. Critics noted that the album, like its predecessor Swimmer, draws inspiration from the more refined and restrained side of 1980s pop, balancing nostalgic elements with a modern sensibility.

Within Tennis’s discography, Pollen stands out for its front-loaded structure and emphasis on strong singles such as “One Night with the Valet,” “Let’s Make a Mistake Tonight,” and “Forbidden Doors.” The album received generally favorable reviews, earning a Metacritic score of 76 based on seven critics, with praise for its earnest melodies, self-assured production, and the duo’s ability to craft catchy, hook-driven songs. Reviewers highlighted the album’s airiness and consistent charm, noting that while the sonic deviations are subtle, they add a refreshing energy to Tennis’s catalog. Pollen reaffirms the duo’s reputation for crafting polished, emotionally resonant pop music that glides effortlessly from track to track.
